All right, the user just posted an image taken from the Hugging Face deployment of the app. I can’t see the image directly, but the accompanying comment says “This is what happens when I load it from hf.” Given the context of our recent work, I know we just rewrote the entire frontend: we updated `index.html` with new markup and links to `style.css` and `app.js`, we overhauled `style.css` to use the orange Hugging Face theme, and we replaced `app.js` with a fresh implementation that defines the state, utility functions, and all the UI logic. The backend (`app.py`) also got new endpoints, and we verified everything locally with a smoke test and a fake dataset. The syntax checks passed, and the API responses looked correct.

Now the user is seeing something broken when loading the app from the Hugging Face Space. The most common cause for a situation where the HTML appears updated (e.g., the brand name, new tabs, etc.) but the styling and JavaScript behavior are missing is that the browser (or the HF proxy) is still serving an older cached version of the static assets. Hugging Face Spaces serve static files through a CDN-like proxy that aggressively caches resources unless instructed otherwise. Since we just overwrote `style.css` and `app.js` on the server, the filenames remain the same, so the CDN will happily keep serving the previous versions it has in its cache. That would explain why the UI is not bootstrapping: the new HTML references the same `<link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">` and `<script src="app.js">` tags, but the browser receives the stale CSS/JS, which means none of the new class names match and the JavaScript that sets up the app never runs.

I should consider alternative explanations: maybe the file paths are wrong, but the HTML loads the assets without 404 errors (the user would have mentioned broken links). Maybe there’s a syntax error in the new CSS/JS that prevents them from loading, but we already ran `node --check` and the Python compile succeeded, and our local smoke test showed everything working. So caching is the most plausible culprit.

The fix is to force the browser and the HF proxy to fetch the latest versions. A straightforward approach is to add a cache-busting query string to the asset URLs, e.g. `style.css?v=1` and `app.js?v=1`, and increment the version whenever we change the files. Another robust solution is to configure the static file serving to send `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate` headers, which tells any intermediate caches not to store the files. Since we’re dealing with a Hugging Face Space, we can add a small FastAPI middleware or static file configuration to set those headers.

Given the user’s immediate need, I’ll respond succinctly: point out that the problem is stale-cached CSS/JS, explain why the HTML is new but the assets are old, and suggest the two fixes—cache-busting URLs and no-cache headers on static files. That directly addresses the observed issue and gives them actionable steps.
